subtitle: From Reserved Posts to Open Skies: Mysore’s Road into the Republic

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of palace balcony overlooking a modernising Mysore city
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV stands calm on a palace balcony as tram lines and smokestacks cut across old Mysore, while a younger Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar looks up to a distant aircraft tracing a line over the skyline.

dialogue.text: In Mysore, a king reserves jobs for the backward, backs aircraft in the sky, and then signs his own kingdom into the Indian Republic. How does old power end in service, not ruin?

i18n.hi: मैसूर में राजा पिछड़ों के लिए नौकरियाँ रखता है, आसमान में विमान बसाता है, फिर अपना ही राज्य भारत गणराज्य में लिख देता है। पुरानी ताकत सेवा में कैसे खत्म होती है, बरबादी में नहीं?

panels.shot: dim interior mid-shot of a public hall packed with petitioners
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV listens from a raised chair in a Mysore durbar hall as non-Brahmin leaders, in simple coats and turbans, stand before him with petitions, their faces tense yet hopeful.

dialogue.text: By 1918, Mysore glowed with praise as a ‘model state’. Yet in the quiet halls, non-Brahmin groups brought a sharper truth: government posts and chances were still locked by caste.

i18n.hi: 1918 तक मैसूर को ‘आदर्श राज्य’ कहा जाने लगा। पर शांत गलियारों में, गैर-ब्राह्मणों ने कड़वी सच्चाई रखी: सरकारी कुर्सियाँ और मौके अब भी जाति से जकड़े थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV’s thoughtful face
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV leans slightly forward, brows knit in concern, fingers resting on a stack of reports and petitions tied with string.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_jayachamarajendra_wod
dialogue.text: If justice is claimed, let us measure it, not dismiss it.

i18n.hi: न्याय का दावा है तो उसकी नाप तोल भी होगी, न कि उसे यूं ही टाल दिया जाएगा।

panels.shot: formal group portrait wide-shot of the Miller Committee at a long table
panels.action: A panel of Indian officials and educationists, the Miller Committee, sit at a long wooden table scattered with ledgers and inkpots, a ceiling fan turning slowly above.

dialogue.text: Krishnaraja set up the Miller Committee to count, to compare, to ask who filled Mysore’s schools and offices. Their task was simple in words, radical in effect.

i18n.hi: कृष्णराजा ने मिलर कमेटी बनाई — गिनने, तुलना करने, देखने को कि स्कूलों और दफ्तरों में मैसूर कोन भर रहा है। काम सुनने में आसान, असर में धमाका।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot onto statistical tables and charts
panels.action: A hand points at neat columns in a bound report showing figures of Brahmin and non-Brahmin representation in services, the stark imbalance clear in the numbers.

dialogue.text: The report laid it bare. A small group held a large share of posts; vast sections, classed as backward, waited outside the gates of power and education.

i18n.hi: रिपोर्ट ने सच नंगा कर दिया। थोड़े लोगों के पास ज़्यादातर कुर्सियाँ थीं; ‘पिछड़े’ कहे हिस्सों के लिए शिक्षा और सत्ता के फाटक बंद थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Krishnaraja receiving the bound Miller Report
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged office, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV accepts the bound Miller Report with both hands, his face steady, a lamp casting warm light across the embossed cover.

dialogue.text: This was not the first quota policy in India; Kolhapur had moved earlier. But Mysore now prepared one of the subcontinent’s most systematic schemes for backward-class reservations.

i18n.hi: यह भारत की पहली कोटा नीति नहीं थी; कोल्हापुर आगे बढ़ चुका था। पर मैसूर ने अब पूरे उपमहाद्वीप में सबसे सधे पिछड़ा वर्ग आरक्षण की रूपरेखाओं में से एक गढ़ी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a verandah in a government office with candidates waiting
panels.action: Young men from varied communities sit and stand along a government office verandah, clutching application papers, some in coarse dhotis, others in simple coats, watching a peon call names inside.

dialogue.text: In the early 1920s, rules changed. Seats in schools, scholarships, government posts were reserved for defined backward classes. For some, it felt like justice; for others, a jolt to old certainties.

i18n.hi: 1920 के दशक की शुरुआत में क़ायदे बदले। स्कूलों की सीटें, छात्रवृत्तियाँ, सरकारी नौकरियाँ तय पिछड़े वर्गों के लिए आरक्षित हुईं। कुछ को यह न्याय लगा, कुछ के लिए यह पुरानी दुनिया पर झटका।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a classroom of new students
panels.action: A college classroom in Mysore shows a diverse group of students, some older and from rural backgrounds, bent over books, while a lecturer writes on a blackboard.

dialogue.text: Mysore’s experiment did not erase inequality overnight. Yet new surnames appeared in attendance registers, new accents in lecture halls, new hopes in quiet village courtyards.

i18n.hi: मैसूर की इस नीत से असमानता रातों-रात नहीं मिट गई। लेकिन हाज़िरी रजिस्टर में नए उपनाम आए, क्लासरूम में नई बोलियाँ गूंजीं, शांत गाँवों के आंगनों में नई उम्मीदें जगीं।

panels.shot: transition wide-shot from palace to factory skyline at dusk
panels.action: The view shifts from the ornate silhouette of Mysore Palace to factory chimneys and workshops under a dusky sky, with Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV walking along a balcony overlooking both worlds.

dialogue.text: Social reform in Mysore did not stand alone. The same state that rewrote rules for backward classes also laid rails, built mills, and wooed industry into its towns.

i18n.hi: मैसूर का सामाजिक सुधार अकेला नहीं था। वही राज्य जिसने पिछड़ों के लिए नियम बदले, उसने रेल बिछाई, मिलें खड़ी कीं, और शहरों में उद्योग को बुलाया।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot of young Jayachamarajendra at a piano
panels.action: A young Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar sits at a polished piano in a palace room, sheet music open before him, his fingers poised above the keys as a servant quietly adjusts a window curtain.

dialogue.text: In these years, the heir, Jayachamarajendra, grew in a different Mysore. He tasted Western music, Indian philosophy, and the knowledge that his kingdom was both old and swiftly changing.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं सालों में युवराज जयचामराजेंद्र एक बदले हुए मैसूर में बड़े हुए। उन्होंने पश्चिमी संगीत चखा, भारतीय दर्शन पढ़ा, और देखा कि उनका राज्य पुराना भी है, और तेज़ी से बदलता भी।

panels.shot: soft-lit two-shot of Krishnaraja and the young prince in conversation by a window
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and the young Jayachamarajendra stand by a palace window, looking out at a railway line in the distance as steam rises from a passing train.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_jayachamarajendra_wod
dialogue.text: A ruler’s duty is moving our people forward, not guarding our pride.

i18n.hi: शासन का धर्म है लोगों को आगे बढ़ाना, न कि अपनी शान की रखवाली करना।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of a small aircraft taking off over Bangalore’s outskirts
panels.action: A modest propeller aircraft lifts off from a rough airstrip outside Bangalore, dust swirling below as a few onlookers shield their eyes and watch in awe.

dialogue.text: By 1940, the winds of war and industry met over Bangalore. Industrialist Walchand Hirachand looked to the skies. Mysore, with its open land and modern outlook, became a willing host.

i18n.hi: 1940 तक युद्ध और उद्योग की हवाएँ बैंगलोर के ऊपर टकराईं। उद्योगपति वालचंद हीराचंद ने नज़र आसमान पर टिकाई। खुले मैदान और आधुनिक सोच वाला मैसूर सहर्ष मेज़बान बना।

panels.shot: conference-table mid-shot of Jayachamarajendra with Walchand-like industrialist figures
panels.action: Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar sits at a table with suited industrialists, a map of Bangalore on the table and a sketch of an aircraft beside it, as they lean in over the plans.

dialogue.text: Hindustan Aircraft Limited was born here. Jayachamarajendra became one of its founding pillars, offering Mysore’s support so that airframes and engines could be built on Indian soil.

i18n.hi: यहीं हिंदुस्तान एयरक्राफ्ट लिमिटेड जन्मा। जयचामराजेंद्र इसके founding स्तंभों में रहे, मैसूर की ओर से सहारा देकर ताकि विमानों के ढाँचे और इंजन भारतीय ज़मीन पर बन सकें।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of an early Hindustan Aircraft workshop
panels.action: Workers in overalls stand by partially assembled aircraft fuselages inside a tin-roofed Bangalore workshop, sunlight streaking through high windows onto rows of riveted metal.

dialogue.text: These first workshops were modest, tied to wartime needs. Later, others would grow this enterprise further. But Mysore’s name now sat on the ledger of Indian industrial aviation.

i18n.hi: ये शुरुआती वर्कशॉप छोटी थीं, युद्ध की ज़रूरतों से बंधी। आगे चलकर औरों ने इसे बढ़ाया, पर भारतीय औद्योगिक उड्डयन की किताब में अब मैसूर का नाम दर्ज हो चुका था।

panels.shot: montage-style wide-shot showing protests, British flags lowering, and Congress flags
panels.action: A bustling street in Mysore city shows crowds with Congress flags, policemen watching, and a British flag being lowered from a government building in the distance.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, outside the workshops and palaces, the British Empire’s hold frayed. Mysore’s people marched, argued, dreamed of a future beyond princes, yet not sure how the pieces would fit.

i18n.hi: इधर कारखानों और महलों के बाहर, ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य की पकड़ ढीली पड़ रही थी। मैसूर के लोग जुलूस निकालते, बहस करते, राजाओं से परे किसी नए भविष्य की कल्पना करते, पर तस्वीर अभी धुंधली थी।

panels.shot: solemn interior shot of Jayachamarajendra as newly seated maharaja receiving leaders
panels.action: Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar, now maharaja, stands in a simple achkan rather than heavy regalia, greeting nationalist leaders and administrators in a plain, modern office room.

dialogue.text: After Krishnaraja’s death, Jayachamarajendra inherited not only a throne but a storm. The British departure drew near; the fate of princely states hung in the balance.

i18n.hi: कृष्णराजा के निधन के बाद जयचामराजेंद्र को केवल तख़्त नहीं, तूफान भी मिला। अंग्रेज़ों की रुख़सती करीब थी; रियासतों की किस्मत अधर में लटकी थी।

panels.shot: mid-shot of V. P. Menon–like negotiator with a map of India showing princely states
panels.action: In New Delhi, an Indian official stands over a large map of India marked with hundreds of princely states, his hand resting near the area that marks Mysore.

dialogue.text: The new Dominion sought to knit these states into a Union. Instruments of Accession went out, each document a bridge between old sovereignty and a shared, uncertain future.

i18n.hi: नए डोमिनियन ने इन रियासतों को एक संघ में पिरोने की ठानी। ‘इंस्ट्रूमेंट ऑफ़ ऐक्सेशन’ भेजे गए, हर दस्तावेज़ पुरानी हुकूमत और साझा, अनिश्चित भविष्य के बीच एक पुल।

panels.shot: close-up of Jayachamarajendra signing the Instrument of Accession
panels.action: Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar sits at a desk bearing both Mysore and Indian symbols, pen in hand, as he signs a formal document while a senior official watches respectfully.

dialogue.text: In 1947, Mysore’s Instrument of Accession was signed. With careful strokes, the last Wodeyar ruler placed defence, foreign affairs and communications in the hands of the Indian Union.

i18n.hi: 1947 में मैसूर का इंस्ट्रूमेंट ऑफ़ ऐक्सेशन साइन हुआ। नपी-तुली कलम से आख़िरी वोडेयार शासक ने रक्षा, विदेश और संचार भारतीय संघ के हवाले कर दिए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a flagpole showing the Indian tricolour over Mysore
panels.action: The Indian tricolour flutters above a Mysore government building, while Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar looks up from below among administrators and citizens.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_jayachamarajendra_wod
dialogue.text: Our honour now lies in how well Mysore serves India.

i18n.hi: अब हमारी इज़्ज़त इस में है कि मैसूर भारत की कितनी अच्छी सेवा करे।

panels.shot: parliamentary-chamber wide-shot of Rajapramukhs’ gallery
panels.action: Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar, dressed in a restrained ceremonial outfit, sits in a dignified gallery seat as Rajapramukh, overlooking a newly convened state assembly of elected members.

dialogue.text: After the Constitution came into force, he became Rajapramukh of Mysore, a constitutional head. The real power shifted to elected ministers; the maharaja’s role was to guide, not command.

i18n.hi: संविधान लागू होने के बाद वे मैसूर के राजप्रमुख बने — एक संवैधानिक मुखिया। असली सत्ता चुने हुए मंत्रियों के हाथ गई; महाराजा का काम मार्गदर्शन रह गया, हुक्म देना नहीं।

panels.shot: quiet interior shot of Jayachamarajendra with books and music scores around him
panels.action: In a study lined with books and music scores, Jayachamarajendra sits reading, a tanpura resting in a corner and a small bust of a Western composer on a shelf.

dialogue.text: He turned more to music and letters, supporting artists and institutions. Yet his name endured in files and gazettes as a prince who accepted the end of princely power without revolt.

i18n.hi: वे और ज्यादा संगीत और साहित्य में डूब गए, कलाकारों और संस्थाओं का हाथ थामा। फिर भी सरकारी फाइलों और राजपत्रों में उनका नाम उस राजकुमार की तरह बचा रहा जिसने राजसत्ता का अंत बिना बगावत के स्वीकारा।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of modern Bengaluru with an aircraft over IT parks and old palace
panels.action: A modern aircraft flies over Bengaluru’s mixed skyline of glass towers, old domes and factory sheds, the outline of Mysore Palace faint in the distance.

dialogue.text: Today, reservation debates rage on, planes still rise from Bangalore, and Indian federalism evolves. In each, Mysore’s choices under the Wodeyars left deep, quiet marks.

i18n.hi: आज भी आरक्षण पर तकरार जारी है, विमानों की उड़ानें अब भी बैंगलोर से भरती हैं, और भारतीय संघीय ढांचा बदलता रहा है। इन सब में, वोडेयारों के दौर के मैसूर के फैसलों की गहरी, शांत छाप बैठी है।

panels.shot: final contemplative mid-shot of both rulers’ portraits side by side
panels.action: Framed portraits of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar hang side by side on a wall, with soft light falling across their faces and a lone visitor gazing up at them.

dialogue.text: From reserving seats for the backward to signing away royal powers, the Wodeyars of Mysore show that the noblest end for old authority is to loosen its own grip so a larger public may rise.

i18n.hi: पिछड़ों के लिए सीटें रखने से लेकर राजसत्ता पर अपने ही दस्तख़त करने तक, मैसूर के वोडेयार दिखाते हैं कि पुरानी हुकूमत का सबसे ऊँचा अंजाम यह है कि वह खुद ढीली पड़े, ताकि बड़ी जनता उठ सके।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Reserved Posts to Open Skies: Mysore’s Road into the Republic
subtitle_i18n.hi: आरक्षित कुर्सियाँ, खुला आकाश: मैसूर की राह गणराज्य तक
